tolerance_rationale: Inherited from alpha unchanged. But the margin is materially smaller than alpha reported: alpha measured heat only and found 5.997790e-10 (~1,700x of headroom); across all five PDEs the worst DerivativeBatch-routed drift is 7.951155e-08, leaving ~12.6x. The tolerance still holds, and widening the PDE axis cost two orders of headroom. Recorded so nobody quotes alpha's 1,700x as the arc's margin.

normalization_vector.justification: Column normalization arrived in v0.34c; v0.22.0 has no counterpart. Permanent, carried forward from alpha unchanged.

pysindy_coefficients.justification: PySINDy 1.7.5 -> 2.1.x. Structure is identical on both sides -- same coefficient shape (64, 2145), same library size 2145, same nonzero cardinality -- but fitted magnitudes diverge by 7 to 10 orders on advection_diffusion_1d (3.6695e+10 vs 8.9725e+00) and kdv_1d (1.2885e+09 vs 1.9405e+02). Coefficients of order 1e10 indicate an ill-conditioned STLSQ solve on the legacy side. heat_1d, burgers_1d and reaction_diffusion_1d are identical (both all-zero after thresholding). Given alpha's clean close, this is attributable to the PySINDy version delta and not to migration numerical drift -- the attribution rule in the runbook.

pysindy_selected_support.justification: Downstream of pysindy_coefficients. Support differs on exactly the two PDEs whose coefficients diverge -- 0.067% of entries on advection_diffusion_1d and 0.177% on kdv_1d -- and is identical on the other three. Same attribution.

residuals.justification: Per-stage atol raised from alpha's 1e-12, measured across all five PDEs. alpha calibrated 1e-12 on heat_1d alone, where the fitted coefficient vector has magnitude 1.000e-01. kdv_1d's has magnitude 4.404e+01 -- 440x larger -- so the same relative precision yields an absolute coefficient error 35,000x larger (6.281e-12 vs 1.775e-16), and that propagates linearly into the residual through |X| @ dc. The residual's own elements are meanwhile ~4e-09, so the rtol term contributes almost nothing and the whole allowance falls to atol. Error scale is set by the largest intermediate; tolerance scale by the smallest output. An absolute tolerance measured on one PDE cannot transfer across a five-PDE axis.
